findings: Deferred queue stores only playerUUID->wall-clock deadline. scheduleInventoryCheck uses putIfAbsent(now+delay*50ms), so another inventory update does not replace an existing earlier deadline in this method. This is not a durable item acquisition log or exact simulated tick duration.

At due tick, lookup onlineServerPlayer by same UUID, call detect(sp,EMPTY,0) if found, then remove dueUUID even if offline. The queue retains no ItemEntityUUID, configured functional variant, recipeID, payment/debit result, transaction nonce or team snapshot. No guarantee about disconnected pending checks or actual runtime scheduling is inferred.

Prior actual inventory listener selects current team using the player context and submits into that TeamData. BaseQuestFile exact getter is map.get(teamUUID). TeamData owns taskProgress longtaskID->longprogress separately from its UUID-indexed perPlayerData and QuestKey claimedRewards.

TeamData.setProgress has no contributing-player argument; it clamps against taskMax, updates/removes taskID progress, synchronizes online team members, starts/completes via team context and marks dirty. Thus a task progress value alone cannot certify which member paid or personally received a particular item. Team progress sharing may be intended; preserve original policy rather than relabel it personal receipt.

markTaskCompleted triggers actual task.onCompleted team context then requests inventory detection for each current online member with EMPTY and sourceTask=currenttaskID. Reuse prior listener sourceTask exclusion; do not interpret that fanout as each member independently crafting, paying or receiving the same item. Deeper callback recursion and max progress lifecycle not executed.

ServerQuestFile teamCreated requests copyData from creator personalteam for a new party; playerChangedTeam requests mergeData when joining another owner party and mergeClaimedRewards when returning to personalteam. Only call sites read here: merge/copy helper implementation and event order were not studied, and no new migration1000credit or oldworld native acceptance is claimed.

Claim path marks reward key before reward.claim(player,notify). Actual QuestKey.forReward policy, external reward delivery rollback, permissions and all original reward types were not expanded; no duplicate reward or exploit claim. Keep original rewards/IDs. Task progress and reward bookkeeping must remain separate from intended-player acquisition evidence.
integration_requirements: Keep material-source and existing prerequisite tasks. Use actual recipe/trade native debit once; ordinary inventory/craft notifications are not payment certification.

For new functional NBT variant acquisition, independently establish full consumer-valid variant and intended player/target acquisition outcome; retain transaction/source/ItemEntity linkage as appropriate. Team-wide progress can reflect existing design but cannot replace that individual evidence.

Do not add a second consuming task or duplicate item reward merely to work around attribution. Applicable1000 variant-production and independent native gates remain unresolved; no production node added.
